verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: the `&(lt|gt|amp);?` alternative in REFERENCE makes the trailing semicolon optional, so an ampersand followed by `lt`/`gt`/`amp` with no semicolon (`&lt`, `&amp`, `&gt`) is decoded to `<`, `&`, `>` even though the comment above claims only markup spellings are neutralized. WHY: browsers (HTML5 tokenizer) treat a named reference without its terminating `;` as literal text in these cases, so a participant writing `&lt` or `&amp` sees it unchanged on the page while the prompt now receives `‹`/`&`, silently corrupting the message text the classifier reads and making the rendered page and the prompt diverge. HOW: require the semicolon for the named branch (numeric references keep `;?` since browsers do decode `&#38` without it), e.g. `/&#(?:x([0-9a-f]+)|(\d+));?|&(lt|gt|amp);/gi`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The finding's root cause is factually wrong. Per the HTML5 tokenizer's named character reference state, `lt`, `gt`, and `amp` are legacy named references for which the terminating semicolon is optional: a browser decodes `&lt`, `&gt`, `&amp` (when not followed by `=` or an alphanumeric character) to `<`, `>`, `&`. The finding asserts the opposite ("browsers treat a named reference without its terminating `;` as literal text in these cases"), which is false for exactly these three names. Since browsers do decode the semicolon-less spellings, the regex's `;?` in the named branch matches browser behavior instead of diverging from it, and the claimed page/prompt divergence ("participant writes `&lt` and sees it unchanged") does not occur. The proposed "fix" would actually introduce the divergence it claims to prevent. Refuted on the stated technical premise.

verificationEvidence.claim:
WHAT: The new `noLiveOwner` guard condition `(status <> :processing OR leaseExpiresAt IS NULL OR leaseExpiresAt < :now)` treats any PROCESSING row whose `leaseExpiresAt` is NULL as having no live owner, so the write lands even though a worker is actively running the job.
WHY: The repository's own reaper logic (see the comment at line ~404) acknowledges legacy PROCESSING rows with `leaseExpiresAt IS NULL` exist; for such a row the `requireNoLiveOwner` failure write (code-review-job-processor.service.ts:190, the BYOK-deferral path) stamps FAILED over the live worker's row, killing that worker's guarded completion, dropping its review and sending the author a failure notice for a review that is still running — the exact #1830 symptom this fence was added to prevent.
HOW: Drop the `leaseExpiresAt IS NULL` disjunct so only an expired lease counts as "no live owner", mirroring the reaper's `leaseExpiresAt IS NOT NULL AND leaseExpiresAt < :now` check: `(status <> :processing OR (leaseExpiresAt IS NOT NULL AND leaseExpiresAt < :now))`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Refuted. A live worker always holds a lease: the claim path sets `leaseExpiresAt = new Date(Date.now() + JOB_LEASE_TTL_MS)` (code-review-job-processor.service.ts:266), so an actively-PROCESSING row has a non-null leaseExpiresAt. A PROCESSING row with `leaseExpiresAt IS NULL` is, by construction, a legacy/orphaned row with no live owner — the reaper's legacy branch (repository line 446) only reaches such rows via `updatedAt < :olderThan`, i.e. stale rows a dead worker left behind. Thus treating `leaseExpiresAt IS NULL` as "no live owner" is correct, and the described failure (stamping FAILED over a live worker's row, dropping its review) cannot happen. The root-cause assertion that a live worker runs a NULL-lease PROCESSING row is factually wrong.

WHY: a redelivery of the same jobId can be consumed while another worker holds the row (this file's own note at 643-648: the inbox dedupes on (consumerId, messageId), not jobId, and the reaper republishes with a fresh messageId), and the rate-limit gate (line 127) and payload validation (line 117) throw BEFORE the lease claim, so this delivery has `leaseClaimed === false`. The unguarded write then stamps FAILED over the live worker's PROCESSING row, its guarded `markCompleted`/`handleFailure` match no row and the review is dropped, and the author gets a failure notice for a review that is still running — the exact #1830 symptom the new `requireNoLiveOwner` mode was added to prevent (that mode is used on the BYOK path but not here). The pre-PR code passed `ownedBy: this.instanceId` here, so this write was ownership-conditional; removing the guard made it clobbering. HOW: fence the pre-claim path on "no live owner" instead of leaving it unguarded — call `handleFailure(jobId, error, { organizationId: this.organizationIdFor(job), requireNoLiveOwner: true })` when `!leaseClaimed`, and keep `{ ownedBy: this.instanceId }` when the lease was claimed; only rethrow when the write landed (or the lease was never claimed and no live owner exists).

The new expression `ownedBy: leaseClaimed ? this.instanceId : undefined` (line 484) therefore routes those pre-claim failures into handleFailure's `!options?.ownedBy` branch (674-680), which performs an unconditional `jobRepository.update(jobId, failurePatch)` — an unguarded FAILED stamp. The codebase itself (lines 642-648 and 179-189) documents that a redelivery of the same jobId can be consumed while another worker holds the row (inbox dedupes on (consumerId, messageId), reaper republishes with a fresh messageId), and that stamping FAILED over a live worker kills that worker's completion and drops the review — which is exactly why the BYOK path uses requireNoLiveOwner: true. That safeguard is absent on the line-484 path. This is a genuinely different problem from the PreviousReviewDecision entry: that entry (kodus-1902-round-a) was about a pre-claim failure being SWALLOWED by the lease-owner guard returning false and the early return; its fix (ownedBy only when leaseClaimed, plus `if (leaseClaimed && !owned) return`) is precisely what creates this inverse failure — an unguarded clobbering write over a live worker's PROCESSING row. verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: The new `noLiveOwner` guard only excludes `status = PROCESSING` (`status <> :processing OR leaseExpiresAt IS NULL OR leaseExpiresAt < :now`), so it also matches rows already in a terminal state such as COMPLETED. WHY: `process()` never checks the row status on entry, so a redelivery of a jobId that another worker already completed and whose BYOK gate is exhausted will land this FAILED write over the COMPLETED row, flipping a successful review to FAILED and (via the same caller) sending the author a spurious failure notice for a review that actually ran. HOW: restrict the guard to non-terminal, unowned rows, e.g. `andWhere('status NOT IN (:...terminal) AND (leaseExpiresAt IS NULL OR leaseExpiresAt < :now)', { terminal: [JobStatus.COMPLETED, JobStatus.FAILED, JobStatus.PERMANENT], now: new Date() })` so a finished row can never be reopened.
verificationEvidence.rationale: The claim is technically accurate. The new `noLiveOwner` guard at workflow-job.repository.ts:248-254 is `(status <> :processing OR leaseExpiresAt IS NULL OR leaseExpiresAt < :now)`, which is satisfied by any row that is not PROCESSING — including a COMPLETED row (its status <> PROCESSING, and its leaseExpiresAt is NULL or in the past). So a FAILED write with `status: FAILED, lastError, failedAt` (handleFailure at code-review-job-processor.service.ts:635-655) can land over an already-completed row. The caller at line 190 invokes handleFailure with requireNoLiveOwner:true on the BYOK 'exhausted' path; process() loads the row at line 61 without any status check (confirmed by grep: only findOne, no status guard), and the code comment at lines 155-158 itself concedes a redelivery re-runs this branch. This is a distinct failure (clobbering a terminal COMPLETED row) from the prior decision's issue (the !owned early-return swallowing failures on a PENDING row); it is not the same problem re-raised. The root cause — the guard not excluding terminal statuses — is real and not refuted by any upstream validation.
